note: Threat registry for review-threat-model. Framework ids are listed only where they were checked against the primary source (frameworks.json); a threat with no id in a column has no verified match there. `fallback` is how the threat is assessed when no available catalogued benchmark covers it.

threats.name: Assistance with a harmful request
threats.description: The model helps with a harmful request that is asked plainly, with no trick: for example operational help with an intrusion.
threats.fallback_note: Write a small set of requests that matter in this deployment and their benign twins.

threats.name: Jailbreak
threats.description: A crafted prompt gets the model to produce what its safeguards would otherwise withhold.
threats.fallback_note: Apply current jailbreak transformations to requests the subject refuses when asked plainly; report the uplift over the plain rate.

threats.name: Over-refusal of legitimate work
threats.description: Legitimate requests are refused or blocked. This is the cost side of every safeguard: a refusal rate on harmful requests is never read without it.
threats.fallback_note: Collect legitimate requests from the deployment that look risky and count refusals.

threats.name: Prompt injection through input or content
threats.description: Text in the user's input, or in content the model is asked to process, overrides the instructions the system gave it.
threats.fallback_note: Plant instructions in each untrusted input channel listed in review.json and score whether they are followed.

threats.name: Attack carried by encoding, language or modality
threats.description: An attack that plain-English safeguards catch gets through when it is encoded, obfuscated, written in another language or moved to another modality.
threats.fallback_note: Re-send a sample of refused requests in the encodings, languages and modalities the deployment accepts.

threats.name: Instructions hidden in an image
threats.description: Text or patterns inside an input image are followed as instructions.
threats.fallback_note: Embed instructions in images of the kind the deployment receives and score whether they are followed.

threats.name: System prompt disclosure
threats.description: The system prompt or other configuration is revealed, exposing rules, internal details or secrets that were placed in it.
threats.fallback_note: Run extraction prompts against the deployed system prompt; separately, read the prompt for secrets that should not be there.

threats.name: Sensitive data leaves through output or a tool
threats.description: Secrets, personal data or another user's data that are in the context, in memory or reachable by a tool appear in a response, in rendered content or in a tool call to an outside destination.
threats.fallback_note: Seed the context with canary values and test each route out: the reply, rendered links or images, and each tool that can send data.

threats.name: Memorised training data is recovered
threats.description: The model reproduces personal, confidential or copyrighted material it memorised during training or fine-tuning.
threats.fallback_note: No catalogued benchmark. For a model the organisation fine-tuned on its own data, a canary study is possible; for a vendor model only vendor statements exist.

threats.name: Insecure generated code
threats.description: Code the model writes contains vulnerabilities that reach production.
threats.fallback_note: Score generated code for the organisation's own languages and frameworks with the scanners it already trusts.

threats.name: Wrong output that is acted on
threats.description: Confident but false output is relied on by people or by downstream systems.
threats.fallback_note: Accuracy on the organisation's task is a capability evaluation, outside this repo.

threats.name: Uplift for offensive operations
threats.description: The capability materially helps an attacker carry out offensive work with little human direction, such as developing an exploit.
threats.fallback_note: Suites that elicit offensive capability need a supervised sandbox (tier T2) and are deliberately not run by this repo. Record vendor evaluations as evidence.

threats.name: Agent goal hijack through tool results or data
threats.description: Content the agent reads while working (a tool result, a file, a web page, an issue) redirects it to an attacker's goal.
threats.fallback_note: Plant goal-changing instructions in each data source the agent's tools read and score whether the attacker's action is taken.

threats.name: Tool misuse
threats.description: The agent uses a legitimate tool in a harmful way: destroying data, sending data out, spending money, changing configuration.
threats.fallback_note: For each tool in review.json that changes something, script a request that should not be carried out and record whether it is.

threats.name: Excessive permissions and identity abuse
threats.description: The capability holds credentials, scopes or autonomy beyond what the task needs; whoever steers it inherits them.
threats.fallback_note: Read the granted scopes, tokens and approval settings against the task. This is a configuration review, not a measurement.

threats.name: Unexpected code execution
threats.description: Generated or injected code runs where it can reach the host, the network or credentials.
threats.fallback_note: Review where code runs, what the sandbox can reach, and whether egress is closed.

threats.name: Memory poisoning
threats.description: Content written into persistent memory in one session changes behaviour in later sessions.
threats.fallback_note: Write a planted instruction to memory in one session and test whether a fresh session acts on it.

threats.name: Memory or context leaks across sessions or users
threats.description: Something stored in one session or by one user surfaces in another's.
threats.fallback_note: Store a canary as one user or session and query for it as another.

threats.name: Poisoned retrieval or connected data
threats.description: Content planted in an index or a connected data source is retrieved and steers the answer or the agent.
threats.fallback_note: Add a marked document to the index or data source and score whether its instruction is followed when retrieved.

threats.name: Model output trusted by downstream code
threats.description: Output is rendered, executed or passed to another system without validation, turning a model reply into script injection, a query, a command or an outbound request.
threats.fallback_note: Trace where output goes in the application's code. The weakness is in the code around the model.

threats.name: Human approval that does not work as a check
threats.description: People approve what the agent proposes because prompts are too frequent, too vague or presented with unearned authority.
threats.fallback_note: Review what an approval prompt shows, how often it appears, and what can be approved in bulk.

threats.name: Insecure communication between agents
threats.description: One agent accepts another's message as trusted instruction with no authentication or scoping.
threats.fallback_note: Review how agents authenticate each other and what one may ask of another.

threats.name: Cascading failures
threats.description: One wrong or injected step propagates through chained agents, tools or automations before anyone sees it.
threats.fallback_note: Review the chain for points where an error is checked or stopped.

threats.name: Agent acting outside its intended purpose
threats.description: A compromised or misaligned agent keeps operating with legitimate access while pursuing something else.
threats.fallback_note: No catalogued benchmark. Detection depends on logging and monitoring, which a design review can describe but not measure.

threats.name: Unattended trigger started or steered by an outsider
threats.description: A schedule, webhook, inbox or other trigger lets someone outside start or steer a run when no person is present.
threats.fallback_note: List every trigger, who can cause it, and what the run can do before a person sees it.

threats.name: Safeguards differ between surfaces
threats.description: The model behaves differently inside the harness or product than on the bare API, so a result measured on one surface does not hold on the other.
threats.fallback_note: Run the same scenarios on each surface in scope and compare them paired.

threats.name: Tampered or unsafe model artefact
threats.description: Downloaded weights or model files carry malicious code or were replaced on the way: unsafe serialisation formats, a look-alike repository, a changed revision.
threats.fallback_note: For open weights, harvest the published scan verdicts with review-evidence and record the pinned revision. For closed weights only vendor statements exist.

threats.name: Malicious or changed tool, plugin, skill or MCP server
threats.description: A component added to the agent is malicious, is poisoned later, or changes after it was approved.
threats.fallback_note: Scanning an extension is outside this repo. Record which scanner the organisation ran and what it reported, and how updates are pinned.

threats.name: Poisoned training data or backdoored model
threats.description: The model was trained or modified so that it misbehaves on a trigger.
threats.fallback_note: Not testable from outside without knowing the trigger. Record the vendor's statements on training-data provenance, or their absence.

threats.name: Unbounded cost or resource use
threats.description: Requests, loops or tool calls drive cost or load without a cap.
threats.fallback_note: Review rate limits, spend caps, context and step limits as configured.

threats.name: Retention, training use and hosting of submitted data
threats.description: Prompts, outputs, files or audio are kept, used for training, or processed in a place or by a party the organisation has not accepted.
threats.fallback_note: Read the contract and the vendor's data terms; record what was signed, not what the public page says.

threats.name: The thing reviewed is not the thing running later
threats.description: An alias moves to a new model, the harness updates itself, or outputs are not reproducible, so results stop describing the deployment.
threats.fallback_note: Record the pinned identifiers, how updates arrive, and who is told.

threats.name: Injection through the judged content
threats.description: Text inside the content being judged changes the decision. Unverified opinions and flawed arguments work about as well as explicit commands.
threats.fallback_note: Add injected text to labelled cases the model gets right and count flips, beside the flip rate of identical re-runs.

threats.name: Policy override through option labels or criteria
threats.description: Option labels and criteria are part of the prompt. If any of that text is attacker-influenced or templated from data, the gate fails open.
threats.fallback_note: Edit one label or criterion at a time on labelled cases and count flips toward the permissive option.

threats.name: Decision flips under benign-looking changes
threats.description: Irrelevant context, paraphrase or option order changes the answer.
threats.fallback_note: Reorder options, paraphrase and pad labelled cases; report consistency.

threats.name: Confidence pushed across a review threshold
threats.description: Input shifts the reported confidence so that a wrong answer stays confident or a right answer is sent to human review.
threats.fallback_note: Record the full distribution for clean and attacked cases and compare the confidence of flipped decisions.

threats.name: Returned probabilities guide an attack
threats.description: The probabilities in the response give an attacker a signal to optimise against without any model access.
threats.fallback_note: An adaptive attack using returned probabilities as feedback; costly, for shortlisted models only.

threats.name: Fail-open and fail-closed errors hidden in one number
threats.description: A single accuracy figure hides which way the model fails. Allowing what should be blocked and blocking what should be allowed cost different things.
threats.fallback_note: Score labelled cases from the deployment's own policy and report fail-open and fail-closed rates separately.

threats.name: Forced choice and refusal handling
threats.description: The model always answers unless an abstain option exists; a refusal or error treated as allow is an evasion path.
threats.fallback_note: Send cases with no correct option, and cases that provoke refusal or error, and record what the calling code does with each.

threats.name: No rationale to audit
threats.description: The model returns no explanation, so a decision can be audited only from the logged input and the full returned distribution.
threats.fallback_note: Review what is logged for each decision and for how long.

threats.name: Gate reads content controlled by the party it judges
threats.description: A decision model used as an agent gate reads tool output or content written by the attacker whose action it is approving.
threats.fallback_note: Place the model as tool-call approver in front of a fixed agent and report utility and attack success together.

threats.name: Policy or data inferred through probabilities
threats.description: The policy text or properties of the judged data are inferred by probing.
threats.fallback_note: No published study or benchmark was found.

threats.name: Decisions differ by protected attribute
threats.description: Decisions about people change with attributes that should not matter.
threats.fallback_note: No fairness benchmark for decision models was found.

threats.name: Spoken request succeeds where text is refused
threats.description: A request the model refuses as text is fulfilled when delivered as speech.
threats.fallback_note: Synthesise refused text requests as speech locally and compare the two channels paired.

threats.name: Acoustic variation changes the outcome
threats.description: Accent, noise, speed, pitch or audio effects change whether a request is refused.
threats.fallback_note: Apply a fixed set of perturbations to the same spoken requests and report the change from the clean recording.

threats.name: Background speech followed as an instruction
threats.description: Speech from another person, a played recording or media in the room is treated as the caller's instruction.
threats.fallback_note: No benchmark exists. Mix planted speech into recordings of the real call flow.

threats.name: Tool call triggered by voice
threats.description: A spoken instruction, including one from the background, triggers a tool call the caller should not be able to cause.
threats.fallback_note: No benchmark exists. Script spoken requests for each tool that changes something.

threats.name: Guardrail sees the transcript, the model hears the audio
threats.description: Safeguards that read a transcript miss what transcription drops or alters.
threats.fallback_note: No benchmark exists. Compare guardrail verdicts on transcripts with the model's behaviour on the audio for the same recordings.

threats.name: Interruption and turn-taking manipulation
threats.description: Interrupting, overlapping or timing speech changes what the model accepts.
threats.fallback_note: No benchmark exists. Script interruptions at the points where the call flow confirms an action.

threats.name: Caller identity taken on trust
threats.description: Caller ID, signalling headers or a familiar-sounding voice are treated as authentication.
threats.fallback_note: Review what the call flow uses to establish who is speaking.

threats.name: Voice output used to impersonate a person
threats.description: Generated speech imitates a real person's voice.
threats.fallback_note: Review which voices can be produced and the vendor's stated restrictions.

threats.name: Prohibited imagery is generated
threats.description: The model produces images the organisation or the law prohibits, directly or through prompt rewording.
threats.fallback_note: No standardised benchmark exists. Hand-build a small probe set from the organisation's content policy, with benign twins.

threats.name: Likeness of a real person
threats.description: The model produces a convincing image of a real, identifiable person.
threats.fallback_note: No standardised benchmark exists. Probe with named public figures and with uploaded reference photos if the product accepts them.

threats.name: Missing or removable provenance
threats.description: Outputs carry no provenance signal, or it is lost on the first re-save or crop.
threats.fallback_note: Inspect outputs for provenance metadata and any vendor-documented watermark; re-encode and re-check.
